references.text: The judge is described in Luke 18:2 as one who "did not fear God and did not respect anyone". In verse 4, he repeats this description of himself, confirming the starting point of the parable.

In Luke 18:7-8, Jesus draws the conclusion from the parable: If even an unjust judge eventually gives in, how much more will God secure justice for his chosen ones who cry out to him. The judge's reluctant admission in verse 4 forms the basis of this argument from the lesser to the greater.

Ecclesiastes 8:11 says that "because judgment against an evil deed is not executed immediately, the hearts of people are filled with desire to do evil". The judge's delay in acting justly recalls this principle of delayed justice.

Luke 18:1 states the purpose of the entire parable: that one should always pray and not give up. The judge's reluctance over time (verse 4) illustrates exactly why perseverance in prayer is necessary.

In Luke 11:5-8, Jesus tells a similar parable about a man who knocks on his friend's door at night. There too, it is persistence and boldness that eventually lead to the prayer being answered, even though the other party initially did not want to help.

In Genesis 18:23-25, Abraham repeatedly appeals to God as the judge of the world to act justly. Unlike the unjust judge who neither fears God nor cares about people, God is the righteous judge who hears prayer.

Proverbs 15:25 says that the Lord tears down the house of the proud but protects the widow's boundary stone. The unjust judge who eventually yields to the widow's demand stands in contrast to God, who actively defends the widow's rights.

In Deuteronomy 10:17-18, God is described as the great, mighty, and awesome God who secures justice for the fatherless and widows. The unjust judge in Luke 18:4, who admits that he neither fears God nor respects anyone, is the exact opposite of this description of God.
Psalm 36:2 describes the wicked: "There is no fear of God before his eyes". The judge's own admission in Luke 18:4 that he does not fear God aligns with this characterization of the wicked.
